_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY — this file is documentation, not a live manifest. cImp never
reads it: the updater fetches the pinned URL in
src-tauri/src/offload/detection/updater/manifest.rs::DEFAULT_MANIFEST_URL
(https://github.com/Dyserna/cImp/releases/download/detection-v1/manifest.json).
It is committed so the schema has a worked example next to the data it
describes, and so the first real publish is a copy-edit rather than a
design step.
DEPLOY FOLLOW-UP (V32 Phase C3 — nothing updates until these are done):
1. Create the `detection-v1` release on Dyserna/cImp. Fixed tag, assets
replaced/added over time — the `models-v1` precedent. Never a moving
'latest' pointer: the pinned URL is what makes the channel curated.
2. Curate the first bundle from detection/rules.d/*.yar (the shipped
seed) plus whatever the current maintenance run pulled from the Vigil
and garak corpora. Version it as a DATE (e.g. 2026.08.07) — the rule
bundle is not semver.
3. Verify the candidate locally before publishing: point
offload.detection_update_manifest_url at a local http server serving
a staged copy and confirm the run reports `applied`. That exercises
the same gauntlet the release will face, including the smoke corpus
in detection/smoke/.
4. Upload the .yar files as release assets. Asset names must be unique
on the release across versions (assets are flat), hence the
`<version>-<file>` convention in the URLs below.
5. Write manifest.json with the real sha256 (sha256sum) and byte sizes,
and upload it LAST — a manifest published before its assets makes
every install fail a check it would otherwise have skipped.
6. Set min_app_version only when a bundle actually needs a newer app
(e.g. a rule using a yara-x feature an older build cannot compile).
7. The `classifier` component below stays UNPUBLISHED until the Prompt
Guard 2 weights themselves are (see models/CHECKSUMS.txt). Publishing
a classifier entry with no assets behind it would turn every daily
check into a failed download and a rejected-update Advisor card.

components.notes: Seed bundle: 19 rules across the instruction-override, role-forgery, guardrail-removal, prompt-extraction, exfiltration, tool-steering, hidden-text and encoded-payload families.
Llama Prompt Guard 2 22M, ONNX export. NOT PUBLISHED — see the deploy note above and models/CHECKSUMS.txt.
